Neither a base arm nor a head arm exists, so the derived added-failure delta is 0 with an empty id list; there is no suite result to reconcile.

findings.text: follow-on: the section done-when's second clause -- labelled-only nDCG@10 stays within 0.02 of the recorded 0.4821 at pool 60 -- is not satisfied by the landed measurement: the fused head scores 0.5136, 0.0315 above 0.4821, and the node's own text says so. The node substitutes a like-for-like comparison (fused 0.5136 against additive-restored 0.3297, same day, same judge, same labels) and reports the recorded baseline as no longer reproducible (the additive rule itself now scores 0.3297). The deviation is honestly disclosed and cannot be repaired inside the node because the reference figure is stale, but the section's stated acceptance criterion is unmet and the coordinator must decide whether the plan's baseline is re-based.

follow-on: the fragment names only the three measurement logs, not the scripts that produced them; measure_signal_arms.py and measure_docs_code_pool60.py live at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reports/imas-codex/signal-fusion-measure/, outside the repository, so the 0.5136 and 0.3297 figures cannot be reproduced from a checkout and will not travel with the plan.

item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to measure the fused signal, docs and code search against their baselines on the golden and discovery question sets; docs/evidence/fragments/signal-search-finds-the-measured-signal/fusion.html:3-9 declares the two measurements, its signal-arms table (fusion.html:14-24) places current_tool (fused) against the frozen additive_rule on the 22 graded questions over the 14312-eligible population, its docs-and-code table (fusion.html:47-56) places the fused head against the docs and code question set at pool 60, and its census table (fusion.html:75-90) re-places the four census answers.
item_verdicts.manifest: read the reviewed run's manifest (status complete); it records tests: [] and test_logs: [] (a measurement node, no pytest gate), baseline_suite and after_suite null, a measurement-shaped negative control whose log carries EXIT=0 and the differing figure 0.3297, and three follow-ons including the unreproducible 0.4821 baseline.

justifications.durability: the diff adds no assertion at all, it is prose and tables, so nothing reddens if these figures drift, and the measurement scripts (measure_signal_arms.py, measure_docs_code_pool60.py) live outside version control at reports/imas-codex/signal-fusion-measure/, so the 0.5136/0.3297 figures cannot be re-run from the repository.
justifications.evidence: fusion.html:98-101 names the three measurement logs and each figure reconciles with the log: signal_arms.log records current_tool 0.7920/0.7182/0 against additive_rule 0.5605/0.5182/2, docs_code_pool60.log records the fused 0.5136, and negative_control_docs_code_additive.log records 0.3297; the band clause at fusion.html:60 is a measured failure rather than a missing measurement, disclosed and not hidden.
justifications.fit: ssfms-fusion-measure.html and fusion.html follow the sibling fragment style, every element id begins with the node id (ssfms-fusion-measure / ssfms-fusion-measure-node), and no file or symbol carries a plan, sprint or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: docs/evidence/fragments/signal-search-finds-the-measured-signal/fusion.html:3-9 declares both measurements the goal names and the two tables at fusion.html:47-56 and fusion.html:75-90 carry them; the docs and code arm is compared against a same-day control rather than the goal's recorded baseline, so the goal is met in substance with a stated substitution.
justifications.reuse: the diff adds no definition; the signal measurement loads the repository's own harness tests/llm/test_signal_search_goldens.py rather than re-scoring, so no capability is forked in-repo, though the docs and code measurement is an adapted copy of the out-of-repo prototype pool_sweep.py (docstring still reads python pool_sweep.py).
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only 29c0d1eda..bd90ae832 lists only the two declared fragment paths and nothing outside the fenced scope.
